For newly qualified dentists with just three months of pay schedules from their first associate position, some lenders offer 5% deposit mortgages. More recently, high street banks have launched new products requiring only a £5,000 deposit with the ability to borrow up to 99% loan-to-value, meaning a dentist could purchase a £500,000 property with just £5,000 down. By the time dentists have completed a year of accounts as self-employed, they can access zero percent deposit options, allowing them to borrow the entire property purchase price without any deposit at all.

However, these higher loan-to-value options come with trade-offs. Zero percent deposit mortgages typically carry higher interest rates than 5% deposit products—around 6.09% compared to approximately 5.5% for a 95% loan-to-value mortgage. Additionally, borrowing at very high loan-to-value ratios carries risks including potential negative equity and difficulty remortgaging with alternative lenders. For some dentists with limited savings, these high loan-to-value options are a necessity, while others with available capital may choose these options to keep money free for investment or other purposes.
